name: n23-natfirst
title: NAT applies to the first packet only
spec: Timeline of a flow through a Linux NAT gateway. Packet 1 goes through the nat table where the SNAT or DNAT rule matches, and the translation is written into conntrack (green). Packets 2..n skip the nat table: conntrack applies the stored translation automatically in both directions. A side box: 'Edit the NAT rule: existing flows keep the old translation until their entries are deleted or expire' (orange). Notes: 'snat to 203.0.113.9 = static address'; 'masquerade = interface address, flushes entries when the interface goes down'; 'about 64k ports per destination address and port: port exhaustion'. Monospace for rules.
cap: Only the first packet of a flow traverses the nat table, and conntrack applies the stored translation to the rest.

name: n23-states
title: Conntrack states
spec: A small state journey. A new visitor arrives: NEW (first packet of a flow, no reply seen) -> reply comes back -> ESTABLISHED (traffic seen in both directions). Side branches: RELATED (new flow related to an existing one, FTP data connection or ICMP error), INVALID (violates the state machine, out-of-window TCP, unsolicited ACK; usually drop, orange), UNTRACKED (exempted via raw/NOTRACK). Footer green bar: 'With conntrack, a rule that says allow established is enough'. Monospace for state names.
cap: A flow moves from NEW to ESTABLISHED once traffic is seen in both directions.

name: n23-exhaust
title: Conntrack table full
spec: Left: a table box labelled 'conntrack table: nf_conntrack_buckets (hash) and nf_conntrack_max (cap)' filled up; text 'table full: new connections dropped silently; dmesg: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet; conntrack -S counts insert_failed' (orange). Right: five numbered remedies in order: 1 find who creates the flows (conntrack -L, conntrack -E); 2 shorten timeouts (established default 5 days = 432,000 s, example 3600 s; time_wait 30 s); 3 raise nf_conntrack_max, buckets max/4 to max/8; 4 bypass with notrack in the raw hook; 5 move to an eBPF datapath. Green bar: 'Start with the first remedy, because it addresses the cause'.
cap: A full conntrack table drops new connections silently, and five remedies are applied in order.
